idea-plugin.name: CmdTools
idea-plugin.description:
Cross-platform command tools for IntelliJ Platform IDEs:

  • open a configurable terminal in the current file's directory;
  • optionally run a startup command such as claude or pi;
  • reveal the current file in the operating system's file manager;
  • terminate processes whose executable names match a configurable regular expression.

Windows, macOS, and Linux are supported. Configure CmdTools under Settings | Tools.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.6.5

  • Fixed macOS startup commands for Alacritty, kitty, and WezTerm (no longer forced through Terminal.app).
  • Linux startup commands now use $SHELL instead of hard-coded bash, with a generic terminal fallback.

0.6.4

  • Fixed duplicate toolbar icons in New UI by registering only in MainToolbarCenter.

0.6.3

  • Moved the CmdTools toolbar group to the leftmost position of the New UI center toolbar.

0.6.2

  • Settings page fits the preferences window width and shows process-regex examples.
  • Added optional "Run in terminal" startup command (e.g. claude / pi).

0.6.1

  • macOS and Linux terminal settings now use the same preset + custom executable/arguments model as Windows.

0.6.0

  • Fixed Windows terminal launch so PowerShell/cmd open a visible window from the IDE.
  • Kill confirmation now lists the matched processes (PID + name) before terminating.
  • Replaced the kill-process icon (no longer looks like a close button).
  • Grouped toolbar actions into a single CmdTools toolbar group.
  • Improved Linux file reveal, Linux/Windows terminal launch flags, and IDE-process protection.
  • OS-aware settings UI with browse buttons for custom executables.
  • Build no longer requires a hard-coded local IDE path.

0.5.0

  • Added Windows, macOS, and Linux terminal and file-manager support.
  • Added configurable terminal selection and process-name regular expressions.
  • Added confirmation and IDE-process protection before terminating matching processes.
  • Added theme-aware vector icons and moved operating-system work off the UI thread.
